definition: The task of assigning a label to an entire image based on its content — for example, identifying whether a photo contains a cat or a dog.
analogy: Like a mail sorter who looks at each envelope and tosses it into the correct bin — bills, personal letters, junk mail — based on what they see.
use_in_a_sentence: Our quality control system uses image classification to sort products into 'pass' or 'defect' categories on the production line.
business_context: Used in manufacturing quality control, medical imaging, insurance claims processing, and retail inventory management.

definition: A computer vision task that identifies and locates multiple objects within an image, drawing bounding boxes around each one and labeling what it is.
analogy: Like a game of I-Spy where you have to find and point to every matching item in a busy scene, not just say whether the item exists somewhere in the picture.
use_in_a_sentence: The warehouse robot uses object detection to identify and locate individual packages on a conveyor belt for automated sorting.
business_context: Powers autonomous vehicles, security surveillance, retail shelf monitoring, and agricultural crop analysis.

definition: A specialized neural network layer that scans an image with small filters to detect visual patterns like edges, textures, and shapes.
analogy: Like running a magnifying glass across a painting in a grid pattern. At each position, you note what local pattern you see — a curve, a straight line, a color change.
use_in_a_sentence: The early convolutional layers in our model learned to detect simple edges, while deeper layers recognized complex features like faces.
business_context: Convolutional layers are the building blocks of image recognition systems. They are what make it possible for AI to 'see' and interpret visual information.

definition: The smallest unit of a digital image — a single dot of color. Images are represented as grids of pixels, and each pixel has numeric values for its color channels.
analogy: Like a single tile in a mosaic. Up close it is just one colored square, but thousands of tiles together form a recognizable picture.
use_in_a_sentence: Our model processes 224-by-224-pixel images, meaning each input is a grid of about 50,000 color values.
business_context: Higher resolution images (more pixels) can improve model accuracy but also increase processing time and storage costs.

definition: A rectangle drawn around an object in an image to indicate its location. Defined by coordinates for its corners, it tells the model where an object starts and ends.
analogy: Like drawing a rectangle around a word in a newspaper with a highlighter. The box does not describe the word itself — it just shows where to look.
use_in_a_sentence: The security camera system draws bounding boxes around detected vehicles and pedestrians in real time for the monitoring team.
business_context: Bounding boxes are the standard output format for object detection systems used in logistics, security, and autonomous driving.

definition: A computer vision task that classifies every single pixel in an image, creating a detailed map of exactly which pixels belong to which object or region.
analogy: Like coloring every part of a coloring book page where each region gets a different color — sky is blue, grass is green, road is gray — with no white space left.
use_in_a_sentence: The medical imaging system uses image segmentation to precisely outline tumor boundaries, helping radiologists measure tumor size down to the millimeter.
business_context: Used in medical imaging, autonomous driving, satellite analysis, and any application where knowing the exact shape of objects matters, not just their location.

definition: Optical Character Recognition — technology that converts images of text (from scanned documents, photos, or PDFs) into machine-readable text that software can search, edit, and analyze.
analogy: Like a very fast typist who looks at a printed page and types out everything they see. The computer reads the image of text and converts it into actual editable text.
use_in_a_sentence: We use OCR to digitize thousands of paper invoices per day, automatically extracting vendor names, amounts, and dates into our accounting system.
business_context: OCR is one of the most mature and widely deployed AI technologies. It powers document digitization in banking, insurance, healthcare, and government.

definition: A computer vision task that locates human faces within an image or video frame. It finds where faces are but does not identify who the person is — that is face recognition, a separate task.
analogy: Like a photographer's autofocus that locks onto faces in a crowd. It knows where the faces are but does not know whose face it is.
use_in_a_sentence: The video conferencing app uses face detection to automatically frame the speaker and blur the background.
business_context: Used in photography, video calls, retail analytics (counting foot traffic), and as the first step in identity verification systems. Carries significant privacy and ethical considerations.

definition: A technique of creating new training examples by applying transformations to existing data — such as rotating, flipping, cropping, or adjusting the brightness of images.
analogy: Like a music teacher having a student practice a piece at different speeds, in different keys, and with different dynamics. It is the same song, but each variation builds a different skill.
use_in_a_sentence: By applying data augmentation, we tripled our effective training set size without collecting a single new image, and the model's accuracy improved by 8%.
business_context: Data augmentation is a cost-effective way to improve model performance when collecting more real data is expensive or time-consuming.

definition: A technique where a model trained on one task is reused as the starting point for a different but related task, rather than training a new model from scratch.
analogy: Like a professional tennis player learning to play pickleball. They do not start from zero — their existing skills in hand-eye coordination, footwork, and racket control transfer to the new sport.
use_in_a_sentence: Using transfer learning, we took a model pre-trained on millions of general images and adapted it to detect cracks in concrete with only 500 labeled examples.
business_context: Transfer learning dramatically reduces the data and compute needed for custom AI projects, making it feasible for companies that do not have millions of labeled examples.
